subject: Integration runbook & token strategy — post-demo next steps

Subject: Integration runbook & token strategy — post-demo next steps

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from the demo/qualification call. Notes below are focused on authentication and operational key management so your DevOps team has a clear onboarding path.

High-level decisions (from call)
- Primary integration style: server-to-server (no user tokens).
- Lumo prefers KMS-backed secrets and short-lived credentials where possible.
- Routing: production traffic should prefer dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive endpoints; embeddings workload can run on cheaper instance family.

Auth & key management proposal (options to discuss during tech deep-dive)
1) JWT service account (recommended)
   - Redwood supports JWT bearer flow with OIDC/workload identity federation (no long-lived keys stored in Redwood).
   - Tokens issued short-lived (recommended TTL 15m–1h), signed by Lumo's IdP or federated via GCP Workload Identity.
2) Scoped API keys + rotation
   - Create per-environment scoped API keys (dev/stage/prod), store encrypted in GCP KMS, rotate on a schedule (e.g., 90 days) with automated deprecation windows.

Other integration notes
- SDK setup: we can provide a sample that demonstrates both JWT and API-key workflows (server side).
- Structured output / tool-calling: will require explicit allowlist for outgoing tool endpoints; include that in the runbook.
- Embeddings / reranker: dev/prod embeddings should use dedicated model variants for repeatable quality and cheaper batch inference for bulk ingestion.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
- <Redwood> Share a first-draft runbook and a tiny OpenAPI snippet for auth headers (attached). (action: Karthik)
- <Lumo> Confirm DevOps contact and whether GCP KMS + Workload Identity is available. (action: Alex)
- Schedule a technical deep-dive next week to go over token rotation automation and sample code.

Attachments: redwood_integration_runbook_draft.pdf (PDF, 380 KB), openapi_spec_snippet.yaml (YAML)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once we have the DevOps contact.

—

Alex — quick technical notes from our side based on the preference for JWT / Workload Identity: 

- Both approaches work; JWT + federation is cleaner for long-term ops. Typical flow we recommend:
  1) Lumo issues a short-lived, signed JWT from your IdP (or enable Workload Identity federation).
  2) Redwood validates the JWT signature and standard claims (iss/aud/exp) and issues a short-lived access token scoped to the requested model and route.
  3) Token TTL should be short (15–60m) for high-sensitivity endpoints; use refresh-on-demand.

- If you want to keep all secrets in GCP KMS, you can: store API key material encrypted and use a small rotation job (Cloud Scheduler + Cloud Functions) to rotate keys and call Redwood’s key API to publish the new value. We support key activation/deprecation windows via our key-management endpoints.

- Routing: include an "x-redwood-region" and "x-redwood-model" header in calls so we can route to dedicated pools (helps to avoid cross-tenant noisy neighbors). For embeddings batching, tag the request with "x-batch-mode: bulk" and we’ll route to cost-optimized instances.

- Minimal code snippet (pseudo):
  // obtain JWT from IdP (service account)
  const jwt = await idpClient.fetchSignedJwt();
  // exchange or call Redwood directly (depending on federation)
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${jwt}`,
      'x-redwood-region': 'us-west1',
      'x-redwood-model': 'embed-large-v1'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ input: ['...'] })
  });

I’ve annotated the attached OpenAPI snippet with the header names Ben mentioned. Happy to expand the SDK samples prior to the deep-dive.
